title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ CLI/tooling
author: Priya Kumar
description:
Background: We need safer defaults and automation for cost optimizations across serving layers. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) sensible defaults and auto-tuning hooks for batching and KV-prefix caching in the serving runtime, 2) a small set of production-validated quantization profiles that the runtime can select automatically, and 3) a unit-economics (uecon) CLI and lightweight metrics exporter so customers and infra can reason about per-token cost tradeoffs.

What this PR does: - Adds an autotune controller that observes latency/throughput and adjusts batching window & max batch size; exposes config knobs via runtime config; default policy favors 99th-p90 latency SLOs while opportunistically increasing batch size for throughput-bound workloads. - Introduces prefix/KV cache defaults (ttl=30m, size heuristics based on model and token distribution) plus a simple warmed-cache probe at startup to avoid degraded tail latency for cold models. - Adds three quantization profiles (int8-fast, int8-accurate, int4-experimental) with metadata: expected latency delta and measured quality regression thresholds; runtime can pick profile by policy (latency-first, cost-first, balanced). - Implements a uecon CLI (tools/uecon) that ingests per-route token counts, latency histograms, and pricing to output estimated cost-per-1000-reqs and suggests policy toggles (e.g., enable int8-fast for route X, increase batch window). The CLI also emits a small Prometheus exporter for rollout dashboards. - Adds integration tests and e2e perf canary to validate SLO/UECON tradeoffs.

Motivation and context: Customers frequently ask for clear levers to trade cost vs latency. Previously teams had to tune batching/caching manually per-model; quantization rollout required infra coordination. This change centralizes heuristics and automates safe defaults while keeping explicit opt-out. See ENG-3421 for design doc and PM-412 for prioritization.

Testing done: - Microbenchmarks across RUSH and internal perf-canary: p50 token latency unchanged, p95 improved ~8% for batched workloads, p99 within SLO when autotune enabled. - Quality checks: evaluated int8-fast on a benchmark set (classification/regression/chat tasks) with <1.5% BLEU/ROUGE drop for most models; int4-experimental flagged as opt-in only. - Integration tests: simulated cold-start traffic, verified warm-probe reduces initial p99 spikes. - CI: full unit + integration + lint; some early flaky tests in e2e were addressed by adding retry/backoff.

Upgrade/migration notes: - Default behavior is opt-in for private deployments older than 2026-01-01; hosted will enable autotune gradually behind feature flag. - Operators can disable autotune and/or quant profiles per-model via model-config. - The uecon CLI is non-blocking; ingestion format documented in docs/uecon/README.md.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring alerting on increased error rate or p99 breaches. Rollback: toggle feature flag and revert runtime config; we have a revert PR template.

Release notes: - Introduces runtime autotune for batching/caching (improves throughput while honoring latency SLOs). - Adds three quantization profiles with safe defaults. - Ships uecon CLI and Prometheus exporter for unit-economics visibility.

review_conversation: Ethan Zhao: Left an initial review. Requested clearer invariants for p99 latency when autotune increases batch size. Asked for safety guard rails and a circuit breaker.
Priya Kumar: Responded that autotune enforces latency SLO by measuring p99 window and backoffs; added code comments and a circuit breaker with two thresholds (soft/hard).
Lina Martinez: Requested more unit tests for cache eviction heuristics and an explanation of TTL choice. Priya added tests and a doc rationale.
Marco Ruiz: Verified quant profiles against model-registry metrics and asked to add tags to profiles for easy selection in policies. Done.
Ethan Zhao: Approved after seeing added tests and CI green.
merge_summary: Squashed commit of the above changes. Autotune + quant profiles + uecon tooling shipped behind feature flag; rollout started on 2026-02-20.
notes: Performance: p95 latency improved for throughput-bound workloads; p99 stays within configured SLOs under canary traffic.
Quality: int8-fast validated for most LLMs we ship; int4 remains opt-in and experimental.
Operational: uecon CLI helps engineering and product teams make informed cost/latency tradeoffs.
Follow-ups: add UI controls in Redwood Console for policy tuning (ENG-3600).
